entry.title: Analyst Attention and the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
entry.summary: We show that stocks whose analysts are distracted by simultaneous earnings announcements of other covered firms revise estimates more slowly. The resulting drift predicts the cross-section of stock returns for three months and survives standard factor models.

entry.title: Inventory Growth, Profitability and Mispricing
entry.summary: Firms with rapid inventory build-up relative to sales earn lower future returns. The anomaly is stronger when institutional ownership is low and among firms with high accruals.

entry.title: Rough Volatility and Option Pricing under Jumps
entry.summary: We price European options under a rough stochastic volatility model with jumps and calibrate it to the implied volatility surface. Hedging errors are reduced.

entry.title: Bitcoin Momentum on Crypto Exchanges
entry.summary: We study momentum and reversal in cryptocurrency returns using high-frequency limit order book data.
